summary: The note defines Serbian as the standardized variety of Serbo-Croatian used mainly by Serbs, and lists the countries where it holds official, co-official, or minority-language status. It is official in Serbia, co-official in Kosovo, and one of three official languages in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is also a recognized minority language in several other countries, including Montenegro, where it is spoken by the relative majority.
one_line: Serbian is the standardized Serbo-Croatian variety used mainly by Serbs, with official or minority status in several Balkan and Central European countries.
key_facts: Serbian (српски / srpski) is the standardized variety of the Serbo-Croatian language mainly used by Serbs.
Serbian is the official language of Serbia.
Serbian is co-official in the territory of Kosovo.
Serbian is one of the three official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in Montenegro, where it is spoken by the relative majority of the population.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in Croatia.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in North Macedonia.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in Romania.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in Hungary.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in Slovakia.
Serbian is a recognized minority language in the Czech Republic.
The note gives the pronunciation of Serbian as [sr̩̂pskiː].
